messages:
taylor: quick heads-up — opened PR <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/PR/47291> that touches routing fallback + small KMS key rotation helper. Need runtime + platform + infra + security eyes before I schedule a canary. TL;DR: fallback routing when model variant unavailable, and a tiny KMS client config change.

devops-bot: CI: ✅ all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e) — 5m ago.

maya: @taylor can you paste the fallback flow? Is this changing eviction/kv-cache behavior or just routing decision?

sam: I'll take platform 👀. If this requires a schema migration we need migration window. Looks small from diff but want to confirm metrics and tracing hooks.

liam: Infra ping — any new IAM roles or network rules? KMS call pattern matters for on-prem/private customers.

zoe: Security flagging — need a short threat-model note and whether rotation touches any secrets in plaintext. Also: does KMS change require new audit log entries?

maya: skimmed the diff — runtime change is mostly a new RouterPolicy switch + a kv-cache-safe check. It doesn't change eviction thresholds, but it adds a cache-key prefix for fallback entries. Should be low-risk for memory but we should run perf on stressed LRU.

sam: @taylor can you add a metric counter: fallback_count and fallback_latency_ms? We want dashboarding before canary. Also add trace span name 'router.fallback' so SRE can filter.

taylor: good call. I'll add metrics + trace span. snippet of the config I'm proposing:

```yaml
routing: 
  fallback_policy: 'variant_order'
  fallback_cache_prefix: 'fb_v1'
kms: 
  rotate_grace_seconds: 300
  client_timeout_ms: 1200
```

liam: that looks fine. No extra IAM from what I can see, but if you bump rotate_grace_seconds we should validate retry behavior against our network egress rules.

zoe: +1 on the metrics and trace. Please add a one-paragraph threat model in the PR description: what an attacker could do if they tamper with fallback routing or a rotated key. Also confirm KMS calls never log key material.

maya: I'll run a quick LRU perf job tomorrow morning against staging with the fallback flag enabled. If it doesn't blow up mem we can proceed to canary. Want me to own the canary for runtime?

taylor: that would be great, @maya. Plan: add metrics + threat note today, maya runs perf tomorrow, sam schedules platform checks and canary window (ideally next Tue evening), liam will sanity infra egress checks, zoe will do a quick security review once threat note is up.

sam: I can take the canary window next Tue 6pm PT. Please ping me when metrics are in and CI is green.

devops-bot: reminder: merge windows available Tue/Wed 18:00-22:00 PT for low-risk changes.

taylor: thanks everyone — I'll update the PR with the metric names, threat paragraph, and link to the perf test once maya posts results. Please add any blockers inline in the PR. :raised_hands:
